newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam keeps the bang out of Tet festival.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam keeps the bang out of Tet festival.

text.p: Vietnam's annual lunar new year festival is set to go off with a whimper rather than the traditional bang as the government maintains its tight ban on firecrackers for the third straight year.

Official dailies carried details on Thursday of a government decree outlawing both firecrackers and fireworks displays during this year's Tet holiday, the start of the lunar new year which begins on February 6.
The communist government says its firecracker ban is being strictly imposed on grounds of safety. The festival is the year's biggest and excitement usually begins building weeks in advance.
A heavy police presence marked last year's Tet holiday as the government sought to enforce the decree.
In 1995 a local newspaper, the Nguoi Hanoi, was closed briefly after highlighting the measure's unpopularity by reporting its harmful effect on fireworks' manufacturers and traders.
During the Vietnam War, firecrackers at Tet were banned by the U.S.-backed government in Saigon, on the grounds of security.
During the 1968 Tet offensive -- a surprise attack by Hanoi's forces on cities and positions across South Vietnam -- the sound of traditional firecrackers is said to have masked gunfire.
